parts:
Not sure what went wrong your description is not specific.

 

You do loose some metadata by converting (e.g. loci metadata are not transferred, as some slots do not exist in the genind world.]

 

To rename your genind from the beginning you should be able to simple use the

 

indNames(genind) <-  “your new names”

 

to rename your genind without any conversion. What also happens that the first and second allele can change when converted between genind and genlight as this is not “defined” in genind object.

 

Also the conversion works only reliably and tested for ploidy=2, if you have other ploidies be careful.

 

Cheers, Bernd

Subject: [dartR] strange results from gi2gl and back again: what did I do wrong?

 

The following didn't work.  Can anyone explain what I did wrong, please?

gi2gl conversion of genind1 to genlight > correct genlight > gl2gi  conversion of modified genlight to new genind2 >>>>

                But genind2 was wrongly changed from genind1

 

More specifically:

I did not have the correct individual names in a genind file.  I did not know how to correct them  in the @tab slot of the genind file (@tab:  64 x 25846 matrix of allele counts) so I converted the genind file to a genlight file using g2gl, corrected the individual names in that  genlight file, and converted the information back to a new genind file.  The individual names seemed corrected, but the other elements of the @tab slot (allele counts) were changed to incorrect values.

 

gi-test <- my_genind

gl-test <- gi2gl(gi-test)

# 2nd column has the corrected individual sample names

pop.data <- read.table("corrected namesandpops.txt")
# correct individual sample names  to give a modified genlight file

 

#correct the new version of gl-test back to a genind file

gi-again <- gl2gi(gl-test)

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> gl-again had other changes in the @tab slot than what I thought I changed.

 

Thanks for any help

 

Janice
